messages:
marta: heads-up — finished the smooth-quant + activation-aware (act-shift) sweep on raven-13b with 48k context (profiled live kv-cache traces). dropping a quick summary and recommended deploy profile.

sanjay: nice, curious about accuracy vs baseline and whether kv-cache falloff shows up after 40k.

marta: quick summary below (all evals on the same evalset of longform QA + summarization + codegen); numbers are deltas vs fp32 baseline. tiny table:
```
Model           Quant    EM_delta  MRR_delta  PPL   tokens/s  latency(ms/token)
raven-13b-fp32  none    0.00%     0.00       6.80  450       2.2
raven-13b-awq   act-aware -0.6%  -0.007     6.95  520       1.9
raven-13b-gptq  per-tensor -2.3% -0.021    7.40  560       1.7
raven-13b-awq+sqt smoothq -0.4%  -0.01     6.88  540       1.8
raven-13b-fp8   mixed     -0.9%  -0.012     7.10  610       1.6
```
Notes: AWQ with activation-shift gives the best accuracy/throughput balance. GPTQ is faster but the EM hit is consistent across the long-QA slice. FP8 had occasional outliers on codegen (razor edge).

ben: can you paste the kv-cache trace/eviction signal? curious about where responses degrade.

marta: pasted a short snippet of the trace (trimmed):
```
# evict_score is cumulative weight of oldest KV entries seen per layer
layer3 evict_score: 0.02 at 38k, 0.18 at 44k
layer10 evict_score: 0.01 at 39k, 0.22 at 46k
# end - degradation in top layers accelerates after ~44-46k tokens
```

ema: interesting — that matches the SDK traces we saw for chat workloads. Suggest we enable prefix caching for the 2 most sensitive layers when deploying AWQ act-aware. small config change: `act_shift_layers=[10,11] prefix_cache=on`

sanjay: good call. what's the suggested canary config? throughput targets?

marta: recommended canary: 5% traffic, model=raven-13b-awq-actshift, batch_target=16, max_latency_slo=2.5ms/token, kv-cache-retention=48k. fallback policy -> fp32-dedicated if error_rate > 1.5% over 10m.

infra-bot: deploy job #4627 started by marta — CI checks running :spinner: (logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/4627)

ben: on the error metric side, EM_delta -0.6% is fine for product but codegen regressions worry me. do we have unit tests that catch codegen flakiness?

marta: yes, added a small codegen-specific eval (synth code correctness, compile+run) — AWQ act-aware passed 92/100, fp32 was 96/100, gptq 85/100. Will wire this into rollout gating.

ema: also check perplexity drift on the first 2k tokens vs last 2k tokens — earlier tokens are fine, drift starts at ~30k onward which supports layer-prefetch idea.

sanjay: if the canary goes green, can we also run a dedicated throughput test on ded-4-gpu pool? need real QPS numbers under warm cache.

marta: yes — queueing a perf job: `./scripts/perf_sweep.sh --model=raven-13b-awq-actshift --pool=ded-4-gpu --ctx=48k --warm=10k` — expect tokens/s ~520 measured earlier. will post results.

ben: minor ask — add a small note about tokenization differences for long docs (we saw ~0.8% tokenization mismatch between our encoder and reference which shifts EM slightly).

marta: done, put tokenization note + a link to the tokenization test vector in the eval repo.

infra-bot: CI job #4627 passed :white_check_mark: — canary artifact created (s3://redwood-canaries/raven-13b-awq-actshift/4627)

ema: follow-ups: 1) run awq+act-aware with per-layer granularity (toggle only top-k layers) 2) try dynamic act-shift (scale by KV hit rate) 3) run fp8 mixed with AWQ as an experimental fast path.

marta: will schedule follow-ups this week. thanks all :party_parrot:
